title: SwiftUI kit: activate with a key on iPhone
summary: Activation with a license key in the SwiftUI kit's gate on iPhone, shown on Diceroll as a labelled fixture: the key field with Paste and the full key, the not-a-key error with the keyboard up, Activating…, key not found, the other answers as an iOS grouped list, and Diceroll is ready with the once-only Keep it in your account recommendation (two reasons, since Diceroll has no Cloud Sync).
compare: The key field is a step of the same form: Diceroll's icon stays at the top with no name label under it (as on React and this kit's sign-in step 1), the art stays behind the glass, and Back returns to Sign in.

Copy from the kit catalog: 'Enter your license key', 'You'll find it in your purchase email.', 'License key', 'Paste', 'Activate license', 'Activating…'. The error 'That doesn't look like a license key. Keys start with pkey_.' (pkey_ in mono) sits under the field with an icon; the field is tinted and bordered in danger. Server answers take the same place: 1d draws key not found (an O typed for a 0: the key ends …B60, typed …B6O), and Other answers draws the rest, offline as a row above the primary with Try again.
The field is filled with no outline (iOS draws no focus ring). The key is in the mono face and wraps to a second line rather than truncating. Paste is a capsule inside the field.

The primary is a bottom-anchored 52pt accent capsule; nothing else competes with it. With the keyboard up it rides just above the keyboard, and the error stays visible between the field and the capsule.

Diceroll is ready: the success check in the icon's place (the product is not named again above the title) and 'Standard · Lifetime · this iPhone is device 1 of 3.' with non-breaking spaces. The 'Keep it in your account' card has a neutral 'Recommended' pill (a fill and a dot) above its title, only Get your license back and Move it to a new device (no Cloud Sync line, because Cloud Sync is off for Diceroll), and 'Add your name and email' as a glass secondary.
'Start using Diceroll' stays the primary, with 'Your license works the same without an account.' under it; the license stays floating.
Accent, type, radii and glass match sdk.swiftui-sign-in.

A visible 'Kit preview · fixture product' callout, as on sdk.swiftui-sign-in. With Sign-in off, as Diceroll really is, the card would read 'Keep your license safe in Polaris Key' and open the portal instead.

Four sizes: the two landscape phones (the key field, and Diceroll is ready, side by side as .kit-split draws them) share one cell beside the portrait key field; Other answers, an iOS grouped list, spans two cells beside Ready at desktop (3×3) and takes one cell at wide (4×2) and tablet (2×4); tablet backfills the row beside the first phone; phone shows the portrait frames one by one (the landscapes hide).

Board copy: the lede is 'The key path, from Have a license key? to Diceroll is ready.'; each caption is the state name plus one sentence; the landscape captions are '1 · Enter your license key, landscape' and '2 · Diceroll is ready, landscape'. 'Floating' and 'shows once' are said in the compare list, not on the board.
Mockup kit v2 (B6, B7): weights 400/500/600, neutral annotation pins (gold means signing only), no glow; in-app kit frames keep the host or product accent as their primary (DL13).

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: the fixture is labelled, the keyboard-up, Activating… and server-error states are drawn, the full key is readable, and Recommended sits where it does in the React kit.

findings.issue: Diceroll is a Godot game drawn as a SwiftUI app with Sign-in on, while Home shows it off.
findings.resolution: Resolved with sdk.swiftui-sign-in: a visible 'Kit preview · fixture product' callout in the intro. It says Diceroll really ships with the Godot kit and has Sign-in off, and that with Sign-in off the card would read 'Keep your license safe in Polaris Key' and open the portal.

findings.issue: On iPhone the frames never show the software keyboard, and the server errors (not found, wrong product, revoked, offline) and the busy state are missing.
findings.resolution: Added 1b, not a key with the keyboard up: the capsule rides just above the keyboard, the error sits between the field and the capsule, and the keyboard's go key is the same action. Added 1c Activating: the keyboard drops, the capsule reads 'Activating…' with the platform's progress, and the field and Back lock. Added 1d Key not found, in PORTAL §4.19's words, under the field. Its caption gives the other answers ('That key is for DJDL, not Diceroll.', another account, revoked, refunded, offline with Try again) in the words drawn on sdk.react-activate 1e.

findings.issue: The pasted key is cut with an ellipsis, 'device 1 of 3.' breaks across lines, and the Recommended pill drops onto its own line here but sits inline in the React kit.
findings.resolution: The key field grows to two lines and shows the full key (22 characters after pkey_diceroll_). '1 of 3' uses non-breaking spaces. Recommended now sits above the card's title in both kits, so it never wraps under the title. The line under the primary reads 'Your license works the same.'

findings.issue: Ready sat alone, with about 850×600 empty at desktop and an empty cell at wide; iOS's offline row was only referred to ('the words on sdk.react-activate 1e'), never drawn; the B/8 typo wasn't one of the characters the error lists.
findings.resolution: An iOS 'Other answers' card in grouped-list style (the four answers and the offline row with Try again, on the kit's .card-answers): two cells beside Ready at desktop (.span-2-desktop), one cell at wide and tablet. Rendered: 3×3 at desktop, 4×2 at wide, 2×4 at tablet, no holes. The 1d fixture is an O typed for a 0 (the key now ends …B60, typed …B6O), captioned 'An O typed for a 0.'

findings.issue: Ready stacked icon, name, check and title, naming the product four times; '2 · Landscape' appeared long before step 2; the lede and captions repeated 'floating' and 'shows once'.
findings.resolution: The 'Diceroll' label under the icon is removed on every step; on Ready the check takes the icon's place; the card title is 'Keep it in your account'. Landscape captions '1 · Enter your license key, landscape' and '2 · Diceroll is ready, landscape'. Lede 'The key path, from Have a license key? to Diceroll is ready.' 'pkey_' is in mono, 'Recommended' is neutral and the errored field has a border (kit). Captions are trimmed to one sentence.

findings.issue: Keep the B/8 fixture and caption 1d 'A B typed as 8.' (ux1).
findings.resolution: declined: the error message names l, 1, O and 0, so a B/8 typo doesn't fit it. The fixture changes to an O typed for a 0 (d2), which matches React.

findings.issue: Add justify-content: center to .frame-grid.devices so the left and right gutters are equal (d2).
findings.resolution: declined: centring moves the frames off the left edge they share with the board title, lede and callout. Aligned edges come first. The ragged right is open space, not a misalignment.

findings.issue: The wide mosaic has holes and captions at six different y positions; landscape frames repeat states and the notch touches the icon.
findings.resolution: One order: row 1 is states 1, 1b, 1c, 1d; row 2 is state 2 beside a stack of the landscape key-entry frame (the only landscape) over Other answers, which spans the rest of the row so no cell is left empty; landscape content is inset 24px more from the notch (.land-safe); the last action sits 24px above the frame bottom (.safe-bottom). Other answers shares a column with the landscape frame rather than owning a row, to avoid a 400px hole.
One-line chip callout; no subtitle; captions shortened as triaged.

findings.issue: Stack frames one per row at full width on phone.
findings.resolution: declined: full-width frames make the page taller; the current scale stays.

findings.issue: Hide states behind chips or use a scroll-snap strip on phone.
findings.resolution: declined: this removes content and adds interaction.
